pr_title: Allow provider sigalgs in SignatureAlgorithms conf
pr_body:
Though support for provider-based signature algorithms was added in ee58915 this functionality did not work with the SignatureAlgorithms configuration command. If SignatureAlgorithms is set then the provider sigalgs are not used and instead it used the default value.

This PR adds a check against the provider-base sigalg list when parsing the SignatureAlgorithms value.

Based-on-patch-by: Martin Schmatz <mrt@zurich.ibm.com>
Fixes #22761

issue_context.title: Provider sigalgs not loaded from openssl.cnf
comments:
Addendum: This is instrumental to have full control over the sigalgs announced by a client in a `ClietHello` and hence would make sense to be added to the upcoming v3.2 release such that the great work of @baentsch can be fully leveraged. 

A PR can be provided on short notice.
@mattcaswell should this be treated as a bug? IMO too late for 3.2.0 but could it be fixed in 3.2.1? Or is it a feature -> for 3.3?

I posted it as bug because provider capabilities are not scanned at all, which leads to the effect that the following line in `openssl.cnf` 
```
SignatureAlgorithms =  dilithium5:ECDSA+SHA256:ECDSA+SHA384:ECDSA+SHA512:ed25519:ed448:RSA+SHA256:RSA+SHA384:RSA+SHA512
```
will result in ALL available signature algorithms to be included in the `ClientHello`, even if the [OQS provider](https://github.com/open-quantum-safe/oqs-provider) is loaded. If no debug mode is active, this happens _silently_ and is therefore difficult to detect. 

It is also not the case that the `dilithium5` sigalg is simply ignored and the other specified sigalgs (`ECDSA+SHA256:ECDSA+SHA384:...`) are used, but all available sigalgs are added (probably as fallback?!?)- even algs that the user does not intend to offer in the `ClientHello`. 

And while @baentsch enabled provider based signatures and hence the usage of QSC certificates, the only way to make use of that feature is to NOT specify `SignatureAlgorithms` in `openssl.cnf` and therefore have all kinds of old, unwanted sigalgs in the `ClientHello` - which in my nomenclature qualifies as bug and not as feature. 

I leave it up to you experts to decide whether it should be included in v3.2.0 or wait for v3.2.1.

This looks like a bug to me since it is intended to work in 3.2.

> A PR can be provided on short notice.

Yes please!

@mattcaswell Where do you want the PR to land? In master or v3.2 branch?

I assume it should go to master and you folks will make sure it's 'backported' to v3.2 but wanted to double-check.

Yes - please target the master branch initially. We will mark it for backport to 3.2. If it can't be cherry-picked cleanly then we may need a second PR - but we'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
On @martinschmatz request I'm taking his patch, cleaning it up (code style, tests, etc) and will open an initial draft PR by EOD (CST).

review_comments: What if `sarg->ctx->sigalg_list_len > OSSL_NELEM(sigalg_lookup_tbl)` and `i==OSSL_NELEM(sigalg_lookup_tbl)` on this `break`? I'd argue it'd be prudent to have tests for these (and other) cases.
Nice catch, I this stems from my reuse of the `i` var for both for loops. I'll add another incrementation var so each loop uses it's own

after a closer read of my code changes inside this block I found a few edge cases for how it could traverse the if blocks. So instead I've moved the `OSSL_NELEM` check inside the if block above it alongside the code previously in this section then separated the new if check into two steps to remove any unexpected edge cases due to fallen calls or for loops.
A test would arguably still be better than relying on visual inspection to find edge cases.
